rfi.title: France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.

rfi.title: Nigeria's plan for state police raises hopes for security and fears of abuse
rfi.description: Nigeria this week took a step closer to a major overhaul of its security system after 28 of its 36 states approved a constitutional reform that would allow individual states to establish their own police forces. Supporters of the move say it will better protect against insecurity on a local level, but concerns have also been raised about the risk of abuse by state governors.

rfi.title: Poor facilities held back Senegal's medal-free Youth Olympics team, parents say
rfi.description: As the Youth Olympics continue in Dakar, parents of Senegal's young swimmers are calling for better training facilities and more government support after the country's team finished the competition without a medal.

rfi.title: Unesco at 80: 'Attacks on culture strike at the very heart of who we are'
rfi.description: Eight decades after its creation, the United Nations' cultural arm is fighting harder than ever to protect global heritage in a world where conflict is on the rise, and the erasure of identity has become a weapon.

rfi.title: French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters
rfi.description: Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.

rfi.title: Suez Crisis at 70 reveals the humiliation France tried to keep hidden
rfi.description: Seventy years after France, the United Kingdom and Israel invaded Egypt following its nationalisation of the Suez Canal, the military operation is remembered as a diplomatic disaster. Friday marks the anniversary of a ceasefire that halted the fighting under international pressure, despite the invading forces' success on the battlefield. Archive footage excluded from French cinema newsreels shows the humiliation that followed, as Europe's colonial powers faced the limits of their influence.

rfi.title: Three-quarters of world's displaced people 'on frontlines of climate crisis'
rfi.description: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN refugee agency has said, urging action ahead of next week's Cop31 climate summit in Turkey.

rfi.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for Shakahola forest deaths
rfi.description: A self-proclaimed preacher from Kenya was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for murdering 191 people, mostly children, by forcing them to starve to death. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult's base near the beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the Shakahola forest massacre.

rfi.title: Tanzania opposition leader Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for incitement
rfi.description: A Tanzanian court on Friday sentenced opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in jail for inciting unrest, after earlier in the day clearing him of treason – meaning he avoided a possible death sentence. The verdict follows a disputed presidential election and a deadly crackdown on protesters, in a case that has drawn international condemnation and raised concerns about political freedom in the country.

rfi.title: Uncertainty over Nigeria vote after court bars opposition leader from running
rfi.description: A court in Nigeria has disqualified Atiku Abubakar as a presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), just two months before the country goes to the polls.

rfi.title: 'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots
rfi.description: As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.

rfi.title: Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France
rfi.description: French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.

rfi.title: Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.

rfi.title: ‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book
rfi.description: Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.

rfi.title: Unicef warns attacks on water supply in conflict zones have tripled in five years
rfi.description: Attacks damaging or destroying water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, Unicef warned on Thursday, leaving millions of children increasingly exposed to disease, malnutrition and violence.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.

rfi.title: MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues
rfi.description: France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.

rfi.title: Corruption in Kenya taking massive toll on economic growth, warns World Bank
rfi.description: Corruption is costing Kenya billions of dollars each year in lost revenue, inflated business costs, and lost earnings for workers, while taking a huge toll on investment and economic growth, the World Bank said in a report published Wednesday.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, manifestations du 7 novembre : à Paris, les manifestants sont arrivés place de la Nation ; la situation est « globalement calme et maîtrisée », selon Beauvau
lemonde.description: La participation lors de la manifestation parisienne, sur le même tracé que jeudi, reliant les places de la République à celle de la Nation, s’élève à 46 000 personnes, selon la préfecture de police. Les organisateurs n’ont pas encore communiqué de chiffres.

lemonde.title: Midterms 2026 : les démocrates lancés à l’assaut du budget du Pentagone et de la guerre contre l’Iran
lemonde.description: Le prohibitif projet de bouclier antimissile Golden Dome pourrait devenir l’une des premières cibles des élus démocrates. Très opposés au conflit avec la République islamique, ces derniers dénoncent l’inflation du budget de la défense et veulent dégager des marges pour tenir leurs promesses de campagne.

lemonde.title: Marine Le Pen et Edouard Philippe attaquent le programme de LFI, que Jean-Luc Mélenchon doit présenter samedi lors d’un meeting au Bourget
lemonde.description: La France insoumise a publié vendredi son programme présidentiel pour 2027. Les réactions politiques, notamment à droite et à l’extrême droite, se sont multipliées samedi.

lemonde.title: Après huit mois de guerre au Moyen-Orient, la mue forcée des pays du Golfe producteurs de pétrole et de gaz
lemonde.description: Pour conserver leur rôle pivot sur les marchés de l’énergie, le Qatar, l’Arabie saoudite et les Emirats arabes unis doivent repenser leurs stratégies commerciales et logistiques.

lemonde.title: En Turquie, pays d’accueil de la COP31, les ravages sans fin de la double centrale au charbon d’Afsin-Elbistan
lemonde.description: A quelque 560 kilomètres de la station balnéaire d’Antalya, où se tiendra à partir de lundi la 31ᵉ Conférence des parties sur le climat, le village de Çogulhan est cerné par deux centrales thermiques au charbon. Les derniers habitants de ce territoire sinistré par quarante ans de pollution refusent les projets d’extension visant à prolonger l’exploitation.

lemonde.title: Ann Jefferson, biographe : « Nathalie Sarraute cherchait à rendre visible ce que les mots dissimulent »
lemonde.description: Pour Nathalie Sarraute (1900-1999), les paroles sont autant d’armes que de moyens de dissimulation. Ses livres mettent en scène des drames, petits et grands, dont les mots sont la cause et l’instrument. Ann Jefferson, sa biographe, qui a participé à l’édition de ses œuvres complètes dans « La Pléiade », retrace son parcours et ce qui l’a amenée à s’intéresser aux blessures que nous infligent les propos des autres.

lemonde.title: En Guadeloupe, la ministre Naïma Moutchou ne promet rien lors de son déplacement
lemonde.description: Pour la première fois depuis sa nomination en octobre 2025, la ministre des outre-mer est arrivée mercredi dans l’archipel pour un passage en revue de tous les sujets, mais sans décision majeure à proposer.

lemonde.title: L’arrestation du père de Meghan Markle pour pédocriminalité, sept ans après de premières « allégations », interroge sur l’absence d’enquête durant cette période
lemonde.description: Arrêté vendredi 6 novembre en Floride pour détention d’images à caractère pédopornographique, Thomas Markle a été placé sous surveillance électronique par le FBI. Dès 2019, la duchesse de Sussex avait été informée d’« allégations troublantes » contre son père par la police de Londres.

lemonde.title: Les prix de l’électricité pour les particuliers « seront stables jusqu’au 1ᵉʳ février au moins », selon le PDG d’EDF
lemonde.description: Le 7 octobre, le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, avait déclaré que le prix de l’électricité ne « devait pas augmenter cet hiver ».

lemonde.title: VIH : le générique du lénacapavir, un médicament qui promet de révolutionner la lutte contre le virus du sida, prêt à être commercialisé
lemonde.description: L’agence américaine du médicament a donné son feu vert à la mise sur le marché de ce traitement, beaucoup moins contraignant que celui utilisé jusque-là. Une avancée majeure en matière de prévention, en particulier pour le continent africain, le plus touché par la pandémie.

lemonde.title: Les mystères du bouton « Eco » du lave-linge : « Comment est-il possible que le truc le plus long soit le plus économique ? »
lemonde.description: Dans sa chronique, Guillemette Faure met en lumière les transformations invisibles de notre époque. Cette semaine, l’infinie complexité des programmes des lave-linge.

lemonde.title: A Rouen, les tensions identitaires débordent dans la rue après deux agressions violentes
lemonde.description: L’attaque d’un bar de supporters de foot et l’agression de jeunes catholiques dans une fête foraine lors de la soirée du 31 octobre ont suscité l’émoi dans l’agglomération normande. Sur fond d’activisme identitaire et de supposées ripostes, élus et riverains s’inquiètent d’un engrenage.

lemonde.title: Que faire, que voir, où aller ? L’agenda culturel et lifestyle à partir du 7 novembre
lemonde.description: Chaque samedi, « Le Goût du Monde » vous propose sa sélection de rendez-vous et d’adresses, à Paris et partout en France. Cette semaine, une odyssée dans la mythologie grecque à Paris, le thème du couple en peinture à Clermont-Ferrand, et un week-end festif à Pantin.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : nouvelles frappes russses sur Kiev, les coupures d’électricité se multiplient dans le pays… les dernières informations sur le conflit
lemonde.description: L’armée russe a lancé plusieurs attaques contre des infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, cette nuit, rapporte le ministère de l’énergie ukrainien, qui signale des coupures d’électricité dans les oblasts de Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Kiev, Jytomyr et Kharkiv.

lemonde.title: Les équipementiers automobiles s’alarment des conséquences sociales de l’accord franco-allemand
lemonde.description: La filière dénonce un compromis favorable aux constructeurs automobiles et craint une accélération des suppressions d’emplois et des fermetures d’usines. Chacun espère peser lors du débat au Parlement européen mi-décembre.

lemonde.title: Au Yémen, 22 morts après des frappes saoudiennes dans la région de Sanaa, annoncent les houthistes
lemonde.description: Après des tirs de missiles et de drones houthistes quasi quotidiens en octobre contre le royaume saoudien, les combats semblent s’intensifier ces derniers jours sur le sol yéménite, où le conflit a repris en juillet après quatre ans d’accalmie.

france24fr.description: Le monde a rendez-vous à partir de lundi en Turquie pour répondre à une crise climatique toujours plus dévastatrice, mais la tâche s'annonce ardue tant les divisions sont nombreuses, sur la géopolitique, la finance ou l'avenir des énergies fossiles.

france24fr.title: Le pape Léon XIV "en forme" au début d'une intense tournée en Amérique du Sud
france24fr.description: Léon XIV a assuré qu'il était plutôt "en forme" et a défendu l'accès universel aux soins de santé à son arrivée en Uruguay, où il doit célébrer samedi une messe lors du premier grand rassemblement d'une intense tournée en Amérique du Sud.

france24fr.title: Iran : l'armée assure être "plus forte" qu'au début de la guerre
france24fr.description: L'armée iranienne a assuré samedi être "plus forte" qu'au début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient, se disant prête à répondre à toute attaque de manière "immédiate" et "sans limite géographique" après de récentes menaces américaines.

observador.title: Ataque a tiro em Cracóvia faz cinco mortos
observador.description: O atirador disparou sobre civis na praça central da segunda maior cidade da Polónia. Donald Tusk confirmou que o caso está a ser investigado. Atirador foi alvejado e está a caminho do hospital.

observador.title: As notícias das 15h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Cidadãos pedem à autarquia para não retirar tendas no Rossio
observador.description: Grupo que requereu o Mecanismo Nacional de Prevenção invoca sentença do tribunal para travar desalojamento. No Porto, pede-se que a câmara mude a localização da pista de gelo.

observador.title: Mais de 450 migrantes chegam num dia às Canárias
observador.description: O Salvamento Marítimo espanhol resgatou 143 pessoas, entre as quais 10 mulheres e cinco menores, que seguiam numa embarcação pneumática a cerca de 50 milhas da ilha de Lanzarote.

observador.title: Seguro defende distribuição farmacêutica sustentável
observador.description: De acordo com o Chefe de Estado, garantir essa continuidade da cadeia de abastecimento "exige uma capacidade logística permanente e um investimento significativo".

observador.title: Carneiro: "Renda de 2.300 euros não é uma renda moderada"
observador.description: José Luís Carneiro diz que PS está disponível para novas soluções no arrendamento, mas acusa o Executivo de proteger fundos imobiliários e pede contas sobre mortes em Portimão.

observador.title: Duarte Cordeiro opõe-se a formação bloco central no Governo
observador.description: O socialista diz que Mário Centeno seria um bom primeiro-ministro, mas apela ao cumprimento integral da atual legislatura. "Intransigência" de Montenegro vai impedir avanço da lei do arrendamento.

observador.title: Os anúncios das casas de moda que vão antecipando o Natal
observador.description: Elencos de luxo, traço humano, e alguma controvérsia para aquecer os motores, e ainda vamos em novembro. Da Prada à Dior, da Burberry à Levi's, os anúncios que abrem o apetite para a quadra festiva.

observador.title: 14h. Duarte Cordeiro rejeita ideia de bloco central
observador.description: O antigo governante não vê como imperativo um bloco central, mesmo numa eventual vitória do chega. Ainda, O Benfica venceu a Supertaça de Hóquei em Patins

observador.title: E tudo Zé mudou: Benfica bate Sporting e conquista Supertaça
observador.description: Os encarnados até começaram a perder em Santo Tirso, mas deram a volta graças a uma grande exibição de Zé Miranda, venceram os leões e conquistaram a Supertaça António Livramento pela 10.ª vez (3-2).

observador.title: 13h. Comerciantes querem respostas sobre o Mercado de Natal
observador.description: A União de Associações do Comércio e Serviços quer saber como responder ao impasse entre a CML e a organização do protesto. Ainda, um terceiro petroleiro se incendiou-se no Estreito de Ormuz.

observador.title: VW congela Golf eléctrico. Seria um “luxo” em tempo de crise
observador.description: Nem o modelo mais icónico da história do automóvel europeu escapa ao machado do Grupo VW. O ID. Golf era esperado em 2030, mas não há dinheiro para isso face a prejuízos históricos desde o Dieselgate.

observador.title: Vasco Peso é campeão mundial de tumbling
observador.description: Meses depois de ter sido campeão europeu em Portimão, Vasco Peso sagrou-se campeão mundial de tumbling nos Mundiais que estão a decorrer na China. Portugal já tinha uma prata nos minitrampolins.

observador.title: Moçambique. Mais de 25 mil detidos por violação da fronteira
observador.description: Entre setembro e outubro de 2026, a polícia moçambicana deteve 26.538 pessoas, 25.117 das quais por infrações migratórias — uma média de 5.308 detenções por semana.

observador.title: Seguro felicita nadadores com síndrome de Down medalhados
observador.description: Portugal terminou a competição com 31 medalhas: 14 de ouro, 11 de prata e 6 de bronze, 26 das quais individuais e 5 em estafetas.

observador.title: Aeroporto da Madeira condicionado devido ao mau tempo
observador.description: O arquipélago da Madeira enfrenta chuva, trovoada e ventos até 74 km/h. A partir de domingo, o mau tempo estende-se ao continente e aos Açores até sexta-feira.

observador.title: Será que Paulo Fonseca consegue ressuscitar os leões?
observador.description: A estreia do novo treinador em Alvalade promete devolver a estabilidade defensiva e a luta pelo título ao Sporting. Em sentido oposto, o adeus do Cristiano Ronaldo continua a agitar adeptos e não só.

elpais.title: Sánchez llama a una votación masiva el 29-N: “La mejor receta contra la involución se llama movilización”
elpais.description: “¡Hasta el Papa ha votado!”, ha asegurado el presidente en un acto de precampaña en Tarragona, marcado por el vuelco electoral en EE UU

elpais.title: Feijóo, desde Valladolid: “El PSOE está a punto de canonizar al señor Puente, qué falta de respeto”
elpais.description: El líder del PP insinúa que el Partido Socialista o sus dirigentes se han enriquecido con el dinero de la seguridad de los trenes

elpais.title: Irene Montero llama a secundar la huelga en su presentación con Rufián en Madrid: “Hay que paralizar el país”

elpais.title: ¿Se mueven las encuestas desde la convocatoria y tras el accidente de tren?
elpais.description: Un mes después, el PP ha perdido algo de terreno en todas las encuestadoras, y el accidente de Urda apenas ha movido el promedio. PP y Vox suman mayoría en nueve de cada diez simulaciones del modelo de EL PAÍS

elpais.title: Al menos cinco muertos y más de 10 heridos en un atentado en la plaza mayor de Cracovia
elpais.description: Un coche irrumpió en corazón de la ciudad y comenzó a disparar a los viandantes, según los medios polacos

elpais.title: Un profesor buscado por la Audiencia Nacional recluta soldados y espías españoles para Rusia
elpais.description: Un estudio advierte de la creación en Vietnam de una granja de cuentas de Internet para influir en la campaña electoral del 29-N

elpais.title: Un juez indemniza con 5,7 millones a los padres de Oliver, un niño que se quedó tetrapléjico por errores en el parto
elpais.description: El testimonio de una enfermera ha sido clave para desvelar negligencias y el uso desmedido del instrumental en el Hospital de la Paz: “Fue el fórceps más agresivo que he visto en mi vida”

elpais.title: Milo Quifes, revelación de ‘La bola negra’: “Estoy cansado de tener que salir del armario una y otra vez”
elpais.description: El actor era, hasta hace pocos meses, un chaval solitario y en plena crisis vital a quien ni ser ‘tiktoker’ de éxito ni escritor publicado había sacado de su burbuja. Hoy, es una de las nuevas estrellas del cine español. Y empieza a ser feliz

elpais.title: Casa Bosc, la espectacular cabaña prefabricada que encaja en cualquier sitio: “Llegas, la pones y listo”
elpais.description: Ubicada en un bosque de Girona, esta vivienda firmada por el estudio Ágora Arquitectura cuenta con manual de instrucciones para agilizar su autoconstrucción

elpais.title: El debut teatral de Javier Bardem con su maestro: “A mis 57 años, me estoy poniendo en un lugar de vulnerabilidad que me hace más fuerte”
elpais.description: Tras una carrera plagada de éxitos y premios en el cine, el actor se estrena en las tablas de la mano de Juan Carlos Corazza, el director y profesor con el que dio sus primeros pasos y que le ha guiado en sus papeles más icónicos en la gran pantalla

elpais.title: Ni Shakira ni Rosalía: ‘Delirium Pepitatorum’, la enfermedad del entusiasmo que desató la bailarina Pepita de Oliva
elpais.description: La artista malagueña que triunfó en la Europa del siglo XIX resurge del olvido en un libro de Vita Sackville-West y un texto autobiográfico inédito

elpais.title: Mariska de Jong, campeona mundial de tatuajes médicos: “Grabar en la piel un pezón hiperrealista ayuda al paciente a recuperar la autoestima”
elpais.description: La tatuadora neerlandesa, que acaba de ser reconocida en una competición en Turquía, es especialista en micropigmentación mamaria tras una mastectomía. Tras 15 años de experiencia, ahora la han empezado a contactar desde algunos hospitales

elpais.title: EL PAÍS alcanza los 500.000 suscriptores
elpais.description: En el 50º aniversario del periódico, que afianza su liderazgo en España y su expansión en América, la apuesta por el periodismo recibe el apoyo de una comunidad global

elpais.title: Hablan los suscriptores de EL PAÍS: “Valoro tener acceso a información veraz, accesible y de calidad”

elpais.title: La marea demócrata abre la carrera por la Casa Blanca, con centristas y progresistas reforzados de cara a 2028

elpais.title: Trump afronta los dos últimos años de mandato como un octogenario desafiante obsesionado con las obras

elpais.title: Trump, de aliado a rémora: los ultras europeos se alejan de su antiguo socio tras la debacle en las urnas
elpais.description: Los partidos de extrema derecha de la UE pasan de jalear al presidente de Estados Unidos a separar su suerte en vísperas de un superaño electoral

elpais.title: Florida, de bastión a trinchera de los republicanos en Estados Unidos
elpais.description: El Estado se mantiene rojo en medio de un mapa que se tiñó de azul, pero con menos votos para los republicanos entre críticas a las políticas económicas y de inmigración

Trump sarebbe stato informato, scegliendo di non intervenire per non complicare oltre i rapporti commerciali con Pechino

republika.description: La società di costruzione Bbt Se ha riferito che a metà ottobre hacker sono riusciti ad accedere ad alcuni dei dati accessibili su internet

republika.title: An Italian is the world’s best negotiator: “Here’s how AI can help you strike better deals”

Lettera del centrosinistra alla premier: “Fermi quella nomina, all’agenzia serve terzietà assoluta”

Extending these flat optics into the ultraviolet could support compact systems for high-resolution imaging, spectroscopy, and sensing, but it introduces a fundamental materials problem: many of the materials used to make metasurfaces strongly absorb UV light.

phys-org.title: New method measures microplastics in the air using an uncrewed aerial system
phys-org.description: Microplastics have been found in our bodies and the food we eat—and even in remote environments around the world, including seawater and ice in the Arctic. Despite their prevalence, little is known about how they move through the atmosphere. New CIRES-led research, which demonstrates a new method for sampling microplastics in the atmosphere using an uncrewed aerial system (UAS), aims to change that. The findings are published in the journal Scientific Reports.

phys-org.title: Future warming events will outdo the extreme heat waves of the recent past, new study finds
phys-org.description: The extreme heat waves we have seen over the last few years may only serve as a preview of what is to come as a result of climate change. A new study led by researcher Philipp Aglas-Leitner from Freie Universität Berlin, published in Nature Communications, finds that future heat waves could last longer, impact larger areas, and be much more severe.

phys-org.title: Light-powered method resurrects 'dead-end' compounds for drug discovery
phys-org.description: Throughout the drug development process, which can take a decade or more, tens of thousands of chemical compounds are produced that never go on to become medicines. A Florida State University researcher is part of a team that has discovered a new way to give some of these "dead ends" a second chance at becoming the foundation for tomorrow's blockbuster drugs.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.
